title: Regions Cut By Slashes
summary: An n x n grid made of 1 x 1 squares, each containing '/', '\', or a space, divides the squares into regions.
statement: An n x n grid made of 1 x 1 squares, each containing '/', '\', or a space, divides the squares into regions. Given a string array representing the grid, count the regions. Note that a single backslash is represented as '\\' in the input.
constraints: Each square contains slash, backslash, or space.
Count connected planar regions formed inside the grid.
hints: Split each square into four triangular nodes.
Union triangles not separated by the cell character, then union neighboring edges.
After all unions, count distinct roots among the 4*n*n triangles.
Connected triangles correspond exactly to connected planar regions.
editorial: Connected triangles correspond exactly to connected planar regions.

tests.explanation: The two slashes enclose one area and leave the outside as another, giving two.
The lone slash does not enclose a separate region, so the answer is one.
